svg.aria-label: and the old arrival-time pipeline differs in the VALUES
svg.text: One grouping, two finality rules — batch as the easy case
identical 4 windows · batch finalises all at event 9 · streaming never finalises 1
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = the grouping column
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the distinct grouping values. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: TOTAL — the dataset's true total. TOTAL = 45
13 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
14 // primitive: floorTo(t, w) — t rounded down to a multiple of w.
16 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest et through i, minus LAG.
21 // function: group(events, clock) — bucket by one clock. This is the WHAT and the
22 // WHERE, and it is identical in both modes.
35 // function: finalAtBounded(bucket) — batch's watermark: it jumps to "everything"
36 // at end of input, so EVERY bucket closes at the same moment.
42 // function: finalAtStreaming(bucket) — the same question with a real watermark.
51 // function: runAs(mode) — one pipeline, two modes. Only the finality rule differs.
64 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the same pipeline, both modes, plus the old
Step 4/0 — and the old arrival-time pipeline differs in the VALUES
`arrival` is the same function with `"pt"`, and now the VALUES differ, not just the finality: 3 of the 4 buckets, by 26 in total. That is what early
streaming systems produced — not an approximation of the batch answer but a different question, because they had no way to name event time.
